title: Stop chasing PAPI Lights! (why perfect landings fail at 200ft)
description:
You are 200 feet above the runway, on speed, on profile, and seeing two white and two red on the PAPI. Everything looks textbook—until you push the nose down, balloon down the asphalt, or slam the landing gear short of the numbers.

The airplane didn’t fail. You fell straight into the PAPI duck-under trap. 

Real airline pilots do not chase PAPI lights all the way to touchdown. Between 200 feet and the threshold, optical geometry collapses, cockpit eye-to-wheel height (MEHT) distorts your perspective, and instinctive stick inputs cause massive floats or dangerous undershoots. Once you master the visual transition drill and the universal descent formula, you can nail a stabilized 3-degree glideslope onto the centerline every single time.

In this tutorial, discover why PAPI lights stop working below 200 feet, how eye-to-wheel height affects airliners like the A320 and B777, how to transition to the 1,000-foot aiming markers, and the mental math trick used to fly a perfect 3° descent rate without any instruments or visual guidance.

00:00 - Why You Undershoot: The PAPI Duck-Under Trap
00:40 - How PAPI Lights Work (Angles & Indications Explained)

01:54 - Eye-to-Wheel height illusion & MEHT in airliners

03:08 - When guidance vanishes: raw-data visual flying
03:28 - 3-degree glidepath formula (descent rate rule of thumb)
04:07 - 200ft Final Approach checklist & flight drill
